Political

System

The

Lao

People’s

Democratic

Republic

an

independent

water,

and

It

a

country

ethnic

groups

be

separated.

of

the

Democratic

Republic

people’s

All

to

the

people,

exercised

by

the

people,

and

serves

the

interests

the

people.

The

principal

social

classes

comprising

the

people

workers,

farmers,

and

intellectuals.

of

sovereignty

operation

a

socialist-oriented

multiple

economic

ownership,

policies

and

strategies

for

national

defense

and

public

comprehensive

and

people-based.

and

defense

and

security

robust,

modern,

well-organized,

imbued

patriotism

and

loyalty

nation

and

the

people.

duties

IX

Administration

Lao

People’s

Democratic

Republic

divides

local

administration

levels:

Provincial

level,

the

District

level,

the

organizations.

comprehensively

assemblies.

the

Committees

at

Provincial,

District,

and

level.

Committee

a

Chairperson(s),

and

members.

The

term

of

office

of

each

Administrative

Committee

shall

be

equal

to

the

term

of

the

corresponding

local

people’s

assembly.

administrative

bodies

have

the

following

duties:

Implement

the

Constitution,

laws,

legislation,

resolutions

of

the

local

people’s

assembly,

local

socio-economic

development

and

budget

plans;

Develop

socio-economic

development

budget

plans,

defense–security

plans

local

people’s

assembly

approval;

Manage

and

oversee

political,

economic,

cultural-social,

national

defense–security,

natural

resources,

environmental,

and

other

affairs

in

jurisdictions;

Issue

regulations

related

to

economic,

social,

and

defense-security

management;

Monitor

and

inspect

the

implementation

of

duties

by

agencies

under

their

supervision;

Manage

Lao

citizens,

foreigners,

stateless

persons,

and

foreign

residents

within

their

territories;

Receive,

review,

and

resolve

petitions

and

proposals

of

people;

Engage

in

relations

overall

people’s

assemblies

a

regular

basis.

CHAPTER

X

People’s

Courts

and

People’s

Prosecutor

Article

(Amended)

The

People’s

Courts

are

judicial

authorities.

Only

People’s

Courts

have

the

exclusive

right

to

adjudicate

and

render

judgments

on

cases

in

the

Lao

People’s

Democratic

Republic.

They

operate

at

three

levels:

first

instance,

appellate,

and

cassation.

The

People’s

Courts

have

the

duty

to

protect

justice,

individual

rights,

the

democratic

people’s

regime,

and

the

legitimate

interests

of

the

state,

collectives,

and

individuals

or

entities

in

accordance

with

the

law.

Article

(Amended)

The

court

system

of

the

Lao

People’s

Democratic

Republic

consists

of

the

Supreme

People’s

Court,

Local

People’s

Courts,

and

Military

Courts

as

stipulated

by

law.

Specialized

courts

may

be

established

as

necessary,

subject

to

approval

by

the

Standing

Committee

of

the

National

Assembly.

Article

(Amended)

The

Supreme

People’s

Court

is

the

highest

judicial

authority

of

the

Lao

People’s

Democratic

Republic.

It

has

the

power

to

review,

unify

court

judgments,

and

supervise

the

enforcement

of

final

court

decisions

across

all

levels.

Article

(Amended)

The

President

of

the

Supreme

People’s

Court

is

elected

or

removed

by

the

National

Assembly.

Their

term

matches

the

term

of

the

National

Assembly,

and

they

may

not

serve

more

than

two

consecutive

terms.

The

Vice

President

of

the

Supreme

People’s

Court

is

appointed,

reassigned,

or

dismissed

by

the

President

of

the

State.

The

heads

of

judicial

panels

of

the

Supreme

People’s

Court

and

judges

of

the

People’s

Courts

are

appointed,

reassigned,

or

dismissed

by

the

Standing

Committee

of

the

National

Assembly.

Article

(Amended)

The

People’s

Courts

adjudicate

in

judicial

panels,

and

decisions

are

made

based

on

a

majority

vote,

except

in

cases

where

the

law

allows

for

a

single

judge

to

decide.

During

deliberations,

judges

must

be

independent

and

adhere

strictly

to

the

law.

Article

Court

hearings

must

be

public,

except

in

cases

otherwise

specified

by

law.

Article

(Amended)

Litigants

have

the

right

to

contest

and

debate

in

legal

proceedings.

The

accused

has

the

right

to

be

informed,

to

defend

against

the

charges,

and

to

contest

the

case

either

personally

or

through

legal

counsel.

Lawyers

have

the

right

to

assist

litigants

and

the

accused

with

legal

representation

and

defense.

Article

(Amended)

of

social

organizations

and

citizens

have

the

right

to

participate

in

court

proceedings

as

stipulated

by

law.

Article

(Amended)

Final

decisions

of

the

People’s

Courts

must

be

respected

and

enforced

by

all

Party

and

state

organizations,

the

Lao

Front

for

National

Development,

Lao

Veterans’

Federation,

mass

organizations,

social

organizations,

international

organizations,

and

all

citizens.

legal

entities,

and

relevant

organizations

must

strictly

comply.

Article

(Amended)

The

People’s

Prosecutor

Office

is

the

institution

responsible

for

prosecuting

defendants

in

court

and

overseeing

compliance

with

the

law

and

legal

proceedings

in

the

justice

system.

Article

The

People’s

Prosecutor

Office

of

the

Lao

People’s

Democratic

Republic

consists

of

the

Supreme

People’s

Prosecutor

Office,

the

Local

People’s

Prosecutor

Offices,

and

the

Military

Prosecutor

Offices

as

defined

by

law.

Article

(Amended)

The

Head

of

the

Supreme

People’s

Prosecutor

Office

leads

and

supervises

the

operations

of

all

levels

of

the

People’s

Prosecutor

Office.

Article

(Amended)

The

President

of

the

Supreme

People’s

Prosecutor

Office

is

elected

or

removed

by

the

National

Assembly.

Their

term

is

equal

to

that

of

the

National

Assembly,

and

they

may

serve

no

more

than

two

consecutive

terms.

The

Vice

President

is

appointed,

reassigned,

or

dismissed

by

the

President

of

the

State.

Other

senior

officials

and

staff

of

the

People’s

Prosecutor

Office,

heads

and

deputies

of

local

and

military

prosecutor

offices,

are

appointed,

reassigned,

or

dismissed

as

specified

by

law.

(Amended)

the

course

of

legal

proceedings,

staff

of

the

People’s

Prosecutor

Office

must

act

strictly

in

accordance

with

the

law.
